title: Notifications whose creator lets subclasses decide

blocks.text: The page's `NotificationFactory` is a **creator**: its `notify(message)` calls the abstract **factory method** `createNotification()` and sends through whatever product comes back. Each subclass decides the product, so adding a new channel means adding a subclass and **never editing the creator**.

items: `NotificationFactory.notify(message)`: create the product through `createNotification()` and return what its `send` returns. A factory method that returns `null` is a design error: throw `IllegalStateException`.

cases.says: notify() on an EmailFactory sends through the product its factory method creates, giving Email: <message>.
notify() on an SmsFactory sends through an SMS product, so the creator does not fix the product type.
A creator subclass the base has never seen (defined in the test) works through the same notify().
When a factory method returns null, notify() throws IllegalStateException instead of a NullPointerException.

concepts: A factory that returns null is a design error, so the null is caught with an exception rather than passed on.
A new product type is added with a new product and a new creator subclass, without changing the creator, where a type conditional would have to be edited.
In the Factory Method pattern the creator's own logic calls an abstract factory method, and each subclass overrides it to decide the concrete product.
